answer: An operator running many aliases as a result burns for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the meadow quota and the umber admission check. Because the counters live in the bridge ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. Submission rate is limited to 2 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole fleet from one uplink. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
